messages:
lena: Heads-up: vendor posted coordinated disclosures for several k8s components we run — nginx-ingress (CVE-2026-0421 path traversal/info-leak), kubelet (CVE-2026-0422 LPE via kubelet API), etcd (CVE-2026-0423 client auth bypass), cert-manager (CVE-2026-0424 ACME challenge edge-case). Need rapid triage: severity windows, backport strategy, and temporary mitigations.

sahil: Asking for exploitability details. Any PoC public or chatter?

devsec-bot: scanner results: https://scanner.internal/reports/1948010001 — found ~23 clusters running nginx-ingress 1.9.x, 14 clusters with kubelet 1.25/1.26, etcd versions 3.5.8-3.5.15, cert-manager 1.10.x. No confirmed PoC observed as of 1948010000.

maria: Quick read: etcd auth-bypass is the highest-risk (control-plane confidentiality/integrity). Kubelet LPE is high for nodes with kubelet port accessible from containers or dev networks. nginx path-traversal is medium unless ingress rewrites expose secrets. cert-manager seems low unless customers use ACME via HTTP-01 + external DNS webhooks.

jon: Draft severity/prioritization suggestion (for discussion):
- P0 (urgent): etcd CVE-2026-0423 — emergency patch control planes + restrict client ports; canary in one region.
- P1: kubelet CVE-2026-0422 — staggered node patching, cordon/drain in batches; extra validation for older minors for backport viability.
- P2: nginx-ingress CVE-2026-0421 — upgrade ingress controller, add temporary request-filtering to block risky path encodings.
- P3: cert-manager CVE-2026-0424 — schedule patch, disable ACME auto-challenges on high-sensitivity clusters as a mitigation.

lena: Agree with that ordering. Private deployments: we need customer advisories + step-by-step patch guidance; ops can't push fixes to customer-managed clusters without consent.

sahil: I'll enumerate clusters by k8s/minor and component versions and owners. Will post inventory here (due 1948010500). Also flag clusters that are on EOL k8s minors.

maria: Immediate mitigations for etcd: apply Calico policy to restrict etcd client/peer ports to control-plane subnets only, update firewall rules, and disable any user-facing routes that reach etcd. If we see anomalous auth attempts we can consider KMS key rotation for etcd encryption but that is high-risk.

jon: Cautious note on KMS rotation: rotating CMK for etcd encryption can be disruptive — only if evidence of compromise. Prefer restrict+patch then reassess.

devsec-bot: playbook snippets for node upgrades/canary:
```
# label canary node
kubectl label node <node> security-patch=canary
# drain and upgrade sequence
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
# perform kubelet package update on host and restart
ssh node 'sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y kubelet && sudo systemctl restart kubelet'
kubectl uncordon <node>
```

lena: Audit logging action: ensure control-plane audit level captures Request/Response for etcd-related API interactions so we can search retroactively. If not currently enabled, enable for a 30-day window and export logs to long-term storage.

sahil: Action items I'm taking: list clusters by k8s version + component versions and owners (due 1948010500); draft patch windows per region (due 1948010800).

maria: I'll create a Calico policy PR to block etcd client ports from non-control-plane namespaces and prepare a private-deployment runbook (draft due 1948010600).

jon: Ops/CS note — Dedicated customers should be offered an emergency maintenance window this week. @cs-rep can you coordinate outreach and opt-ins?

cs-rep: I'll prepare an advisory template and reach out to Dedicated contacts; include optional emergency window scheduling.

lena: Who can lead the overnight canary? @oncall-tim can you take the midnight AZ-staggered patch wave? We want 30m gaps between AZs and a rollback plan.

oncall-tim: I can run it. Propose start 00:30 UTC, 30m stagger, run health checks after each AZ (etcd cluster health, API latency, control-plane metrics). I'll create an incident channel and post status updates.

devsec-bot: created incident channel #sec-patch-1948009999

maria: For nginx ingress, temporary mitigation: add ingress snippet to reject encoded slashes and suspicious path characters; push to canary ingress before cluster-wide release. Also validate ingress rules that mount secrets.

jon: Note on cert-manager: the patch will likely be a helm chart bump and may require CRD migration for clusters <1.8 — include migration steps in release notes and runbook.

lena: Final call for now: execute P0 (etcd) tonight for control planes only with network restrictions + single-cluster canary. P1 (kubelet) will start tomorrow night in a staged rollout. We'll publish an internal advisory and customer notice after patch windows are locked. :thumbsup:

oncall-tim: Acknowledged. Will update #sec-patch-1948009999 with progress, rollbacks, and telemetry.

sahil: Thanks all — I'll post the inventory and schedule into this thread when ready.
